proof:
Source and role. This is a trace-type estimate obtained by integrating along rays from the origin; in textbook proofs of the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem the same boundary control comes from an extension operator (Evans 5.7; Gilbarg-Trudinger 7.10). It gives the uniform smallness of the L^2 mass near the sphere needed by the sibling w12_ball_rellich_compactness, which is fact (R) of the parent proof. It uses the sibling Submission.w12_ball_smooth_approximation, called (A): for IsW12WithGradient f g B and 0 < s < 1 there are C^infinity functions phi_j with int_{B_s}|phi_j - f|^2 -> 0 and int_{B_s}|grad phi_j - g|^2 -> 0.

Notation as in (A); all integrals of nonnegative functions are lintegrals. Set C := 2^{n+3} and a := sqrt(1-r), which lies in (0,1).

Proof.
0. Measurability. As in (A), assume f and g are strongly measurable; representatives that agree a.e. on B change nothing.

1. Trivial range. If r < 1/2 then a > 1/sqrt 2, so C a >= 2^{n+3}/sqrt 2 >= 1, and int_{B \ B_r} |f|^2 <= int_B |f|^2 <= C a (int_B |f|^2 + int_B |g|^2). From now on assume 1/2 <= r < 1 and put tau := 1 - a/2. Then 1/2 <= tau < 1, 1 - tau = a/2, and tau^{-n} <= 2^n.

2. Smooth estimate. Let phi be in C^1(R^n), 0 < s <= 1, and A_s := B_s \ B_{rs} = {x : rs <= |x| < s}. Then int_{A_s} |phi|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a (int_{B_s} |phi|^2 + int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2).
(a) Pointwise. For |x| <= 1 and t in [tau,1], phi(x) - phi(tx) = int_t^1 <grad phi(sigma x), x> dsigma. Use (p+q)^2 <= 2p^2 + 2q^2, Cauchy-Schwarz on [t,1] (whose length is <= 1 - tau), and |x| <= 1:
|phi(x)|^2 <= 2|phi(tx)|^2 + 2(1-tau) int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dsigma.
(b) Averaging (a) over t in [tau,1]:
|phi(x)|^2 <= (2/(1-tau)) int_tau^1 |phi(tx)|^2 dt + 2(1-tau) int_tau^1 |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dsigma.
(c) Integrate (b) over x in A_s (a subset of closedBall(0,1)) and swap the integrals by Tonelli.
First term. Fix t in [tau,1]. The substitution y = tx (Jacobian t^n) gives int_{A_s} |phi(tx)|^2 dx = t^{-n} int_{tA_s} |phi(y)|^2 dy, where tA_s = {y : rst <= |y| < st}. Hence
int_tau^1 int_{A_s} |phi(tx)|^2 dx dt = int |phi(y)|^2 (int_tau^1 t^{-n} 1[rst <= |y| < st] dt) dy.
If |y| >= s, no t <= 1 satisfies |y| < st. If |y| < s, the admissible t lie in (|y|/s, |y|/(rs)], an interval of length (|y|/s)(1/r - 1) <= (1-r)/r <= 2(1-r); also t^{-n} <= 2^n. So the inner integral is <= 2^{n+1}(1-r) 1_{B_s}(y). The first term is therefore <= (2/(1-tau)) 2^{n+1} (1-r) int_{B_s} |phi|^2 = (4/a) 2^{n+1} a^2 int_{B_s} |phi|^2 = 2^{n+3} a int_{B_s} |phi|^2.
Second term. For fixed sigma in [tau,1], int_{A_s} |grad phi(sigma x)|^2 dx = sigma^{-n} int_{sigma A_s} |grad phi|^2 <= 2^n int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2, because sigma A_s lies in B_{sigma s}, inside B_s. So the second term is <= 2(1-tau)(1-tau) 2^n int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2 = 2^{n-1} a^2 int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a int_{B_s} |grad phi|^2, as a <= 1.
Adding the two terms proves the smooth estimate.

3. Passage to f on B_s, for 0 < s < 1. By (A) with radius s, choose C^infinity phi_j with ||phi_j - f||_{2,B_s} -> 0 and ||grad phi_j - g||_{2,B_s} -> 0. By Minkowski the L^2 norms converge: int_{A_s} |phi_j|^2 -> int_{A_s} |f|^2 (A_s lies in B_s), int_{B_s} |phi_j|^2 -> int_{B_s} |f|^2, and int_{B_s} |grad phi_j|^2 -> int_{B_s} |g|^2, all finite. Letting j -> infinity in step 2 applied to phi_j:
int_{A_s} |f|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a (int_{B_s} |f|^2 + int_{B_s} |g|^2) <= 2^{n+3} a (int_B |f|^2 + int_B |g|^2).

4. s -> 1. Since B_{rs} lies in B_r, the set B_s \ B_r lies in A_s. So int_{B_s \ B_r} |f|^2 <= 2^{n+3} a (int_B |f|^2 + int_B |g|^2) for every s in (0,1). Along s_m := 1 - 1/(m+2) the sets B_s \ B_r increase to B \ B_r, so monotone convergence gives int_{B \ B_r} |f|^2 <= 2^{n+3} sqrt(1-r) (int_B |f|^2 + int_B |g|^2). This is the claim with C = 2^{n+3}; in Lean the right side is ENNReal.ofReal (C * sqrt(1-r)) times the sum of the two lintegrals. QED
